revisions.title: A proposal under pressure
revisions.body: Hear this section as a stress test for participation, not as a catalogue of rival definitions. The whole-in-many proposal would make the one Form separate from itself; the part-in-many proposal makes the Form divisible and yields absurdities for largeness, equality, and smallness. When Socrates shifts from Forms as thoughts to Forms as paradigms, hear that as another attempt to save the account—not yet as a solution.

revisions.title: The One in Time
revisions.body: Here “is” is tied to the present, while “was” and “will be” belong to past and future. The One then becomes older and younger than itself, yet also neither, depending on whether we follow becoming or equal duration. From 153a, comparable results appear between the One and the others. One way to read this sequence is as a test of temporal descriptions, not a single settled chronology.
